text:
ashley: FYI support escalation — multiple customers reporting p99 latency spikes on /v1/generate in eu-west-1 starting ~11:03 UTC. Customers: corp-alpha, edu-labs. Tagging oncall.

oncall-bot: Incident INC-2389 created and paged. Priority: P1 if customers are degraded.

kai: Looking at dashboards now — p95 mostly fine (~250ms) but p99 jumped from ~800ms to ~2200ms across models in eu-west-1. QPS hasn't increased. Traces show long queue_time on inference pods.

ashley: There was an automated model rollout last night: gptx-2-8bit rolled to eu-west-1 at 02:10 UTC (can confirm with deploy history).

ved: Correlating traces to rollout — KV cache miss rate for gptx-2-8bit spiked from 8% to ~60%. Worker memory pressure also increased; GC/oom-kills not reported but swap activity up. Likely kernel/pageing and increased latency per request.

kai: Quick mitigation plan (short-lived):
1) Apply circuit breaker to route requests for tier=free and tier=trial to fallback model gptx-1-16b in eu-west-1.
2) Enforce temporary per-key rate limit (50 r/s) for affected tenants to reduce queuing.
3) Shift non-enterprise traffic for eu-west-1 to us-east-1 for 30m while we investigate.
4) If rollback safe, roll back gptx-2-8bit rollout in eu-west-1.

ashley: I can run the traffic-shift and rate limit now. Need the exact redwoodctl commands.

kai: Run these — adjust tenant labels as needed (paste into admin shell):

```
# shift traffic for non-enterprise to us-east-1
redwoodctl routes update --route /v1/generate \ 
  --selector "tier in (free,trial) AND region==eu-west-1" \ 
  --traffic '{"eu-west-1":0.0,"us-east-1":1.0}'

# apply temporary per-key rate limit
redwoodctl rate-limits set --selector "tenant in (corp-alpha,edu-labs)" --limit 50

# enable circuit breaker fallback for the route
redwoodctl policies set --route /v1/generate --policy '{"circuit_breaker": {"error_threshold": 0.2, "latency_ms": 1000}, "fallback_model": "gptx-1-16b"}'
```

ved: Also consider enabling prefix/KV caching aggressively (TTL 10m) for the affected models to reduce backend load. Config snippet to toggle caching:

```
# enable KV cache for model gptx-2-8bit
redwoodctl model-config set gptx-2-8bit --kv-cache enabled --kv-ttl 600
```

kai: If we need a faster, less risky mitigation: set a soft p99 SLO guardrail that returns a lightweight response (cached stub or short model) when request latency would exceed 1200ms. This is degradable but keeps clients alive.

ashley: Executed traffic-shift + rate-limits now. Moving trial/free -> us-east-1, rate-limit applied to corp-alpha & edu-labs. Waiting 60s for metrics to stabilize.

support-bot: Noted — customers notified via support tickets with temporary mitigation summary and ETA 30m.

ashley: Metrics update: p99 in eu-west-1 dropped from 2200ms -> 900ms after traffic shift; overall customer impact reduced. Queue_time and KV-miss trending down.

ved: Next steps for root cause: 1) reproduce locally with gptx-2-8bit using live workload (trace sampling), 2) run memory profiling on workers, 3) validate quantization path kernel selection for eu-west-1 hardware. If repro consistent, schedule rollback of gptx-2-8bit and reopen rollout plan with increased canary sample sizes.

kai: For postmortem and playbook updates: add explicit SLO guardrail entries for p95/p99 that wire into automatic fallback policies (rate-limit -> cb -> model-fallback -> region-failover). Also add a checklist to verify KV-cache config after model rollouts.

ashley: I'll create the incident ticket and link trace IDs + command history. Marking this thread as the mitigation chat. Reassigning to eng-runtime for deeper fix (ved + kai).

ved: tagging eng-runtime and eng-ml for triage. Good catch.

ashley: closing the immediate escalation — leaving monitoring alerts on for 6 hours. If p99 creeps back up, we'll re-open. :white_check_mark:
